definitions.explanation: A Buddhist monk, especially a wandering one in older times. Now mainly historical and in names and set compounds.

examples.japanese: {琵琶法師|びわほうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{平家物語|へいけものがたり}→平家物語：31060_heikemonogatari⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{語|かた}った→語る：01930_kataru⟧。
examples.english: A biwa-playing monk recited the Tale of the Heike.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔話|むかしばなし}→昔話：12718_mukashibanashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{旅|たび}→旅：03407_tabi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{法師|ほうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{出|で}てくる→出てくる：29121_detekuru⟧。
examples.english: Traveling monks often appear in old folk tales.

examples.japanese: {西行法師|さいぎょうほうし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{各地|かくち}→各地：00155_kakuchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{旅|たび}→旅：03407_tabi⟧し⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{和歌|わか}→和歌：05230_waka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詠|よ}んだ→詠む：14186_yomu⟧。
examples.english: The monk Saigyō composed many waka poems as he traveled around the country.

notes:
Historical and literary. In everyday speech a monk is お{坊|ぼう}さん or ⟦{僧侶|そうりょ}→僧侶：11529_souryo⟧.

COMPOUNDS:
- {琵琶法師|びわほうし}: blind monk who recited tales to the biwa lute
- ⟦{一寸法師|いっすんぼうし}→一寸法師：24967_issunboushi⟧: Issun-bōshi, the inch-high hero of a folk tale
- {影法師|かげぼうし}: a person's shadow or silhouette

PRONUNCIATION:
In some compounds the word becomes ぼうし (⟦{一寸法師|いっすんぼうし}→一寸法師：24967_issunboushi⟧, {影法師|かげぼうし}). Do not confuse it with ⟦{帽子|ぼうし}→帽子：00692_boushi⟧ (hat) or ⟦{奉仕|ほうし}→奉仕：17413_houshi⟧ (service).
